chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a man who becomes heedless in the two rakʿahs and speaks, he said: He completes what remains of his salat (prayer), whether he spoke or did not speak, and there is nothing upon him. So this does not contradict the first report concerning the obligation of the two sajdahs of forgetfulness, because there is nothing in the report stating that the two sajdahs of forgetfulness are not upon him. Rather, it only says that there is nothing upon him, and it is possible that this is an indication to something other than that, such as sin and burden.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs under discussion in the prayer
key_terms.الْخَبَرَ الْأَوَّلَ: the earlier hadith report being reconciled with this one
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness in prayer
key_terms.يَسْهُو: becomes forgetful or inattentive during the prayer

ai.seo_question: Does speaking forgetfully during salat (prayer) invalidate the prayer or require sajdatay al-sahw?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of one who speaks forgetfully during salat (prayer), stating that he should complete the remainder of his prayer. The text then clarifies that saying 'there is nothing upon him' does not negate the obligation of sajdatay al-sahw, and may instead mean that there is no sin or blame upon him.
